claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.
- France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence: Political tension grips France after rioting marred protests over the cost of living and struggling public services, Katya Adler writes.
- Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured: Prime Minister Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".
- Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia: Two men tell of the work they say they have been doing to support Ukrainian intelligence during the war.
- Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.
- Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting in Mumbai: Video published by several news outlets shows gunmen firing multiple shots at a car while it is moving past a crowd.
- Kenya pastor accused of ordering parents to starve their children to death faces verdict: Prosecutors say Paul Mackenzie lured the latest victims to their deaths by writing notes from his prison cell.
- Bomb threat forces Israel to Austria flight into emergency landing: The Airbus jet landed safely in Bulgaria and all passengers and crew aboard were unharmed, officials said.
- Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.
- Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to 'public benefit fund': The announcement comes as Anthropic lays the ground for a blockbuster stock market listing.
- EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.
- Australian Greens senator denies claims of misconduct towards women: Jordon Steele-John says the timing of the claims is motivated by "nasty political games" within the Greens.

image_provider.prompt: A fractured cityscape at dusk with buildings split vertically down the center—one half engulfed in flames and chaos (rioting figures, smoke, overturned vehicles), the other half eerily calm and ordered with clean lines and muted tones. A central figure stands at the divide, arms outstretched but unable to bridge the gap. Heavy use of red and orange against cool grays. Bold geometric shapes, strong chiaroscuro contrast, modernist composition inspired by cold war propaganda art but inverted—the divide is not geographical but social. Pixelated, high-contrast, dreamlike.
